Leckava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšiai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Leckava's Jewish community, settled in the 18th century, reached 70 percent of the population by 1897. (The source record's own account contains an apparent inconsistency here, briefly mentioning the population decline of a different town, Židikai, mid-narrative — likely a copy-paste error rather than a fact about Leckava itself.) Religious and communal life centered on a single wooden Beit Midrash, and continued even during Soviet rule from 1940 to 1941, by which point only 10 Jewish families remained. After the German invasion, Lithuanian nationalists arrested the town's Jews — including the elderly, women, and children — and transported them to Mažeikiai, where all were murdered on August 5, 1941, alongside Jews from the surrounding region.
